Description

The Global Services NPDI Project Manager is responsible for leading and coordinating New Product Development and Introduction (NPDI) initiatives that enable the successful launch, service readiness, and global deployment of Vertiv products and service offerings.

This role partners with Global Services, Product Management, Engineering, Operations, and regional service organizations to ensure that service requirements are incorporated into product development, design transfer, and launch activities. The Project Manager provides end-to-end project leadership, governance, and execution oversight across Hardware + Services NPDI and Service-Only NPDI initiatives.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, execution-oriented leader who can manage complex, cross-functional programs, identify risks, drive accountability, and translate product and technology initiatives into scalable global service capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

Global Services NPDI Project Leadership
Lead assigned Hardware + Services NPDI and Service-Only NPDI projects from intake through launch and service readiness.
Establish project scope, objectives, timelines, milestones, deliverables, and success criteria.
Coordinate cross-functional teams across Global Services, Product Management, Engineering, Operations, and regional organizations.
Ensure projects align with business priorities, service strategy, and global deployment requirements.
Manage multiple concurrent projects across Vertiv’s business units and product portfolios.
Drive project execution and accountability across geographically distributed teams.
NPDI Governance and Stage-Gate Management
Lead Global Services participation in NPDI governance and stage-gate activities.
Ensure service requirements, risks, dependencies, and readiness activities are identified and addressed throughout the project lifecycle.
Coordinate project reviews, status updates, and gate readiness assessments.
Track required deliverables and ensure appropriate Global Services assessments are completed.
Partner with BU PMO leads and Product Managers to align project priorities, ownership, and governance expectations.
Escalate risks, issues, and decisions requiring leadership attention.
Service Readiness and Launch Execution
Develop and manage service readiness plans for new products, technologies, and service offerings.
Coordinate readiness activities involving technical documentation, service procedures, training, tools, spare parts, systems, and regional capabilities.
Partner with NPDI Engineers and regional service teams to identify and close readiness gaps.
Ensure service deliverables are aligned with product launch and deployment timelines.
Support design transfer, product introduction, and global service implementation initiatives.
Establish launch readiness criteria and monitor progress through implementation and stabilization.
Portfolio and Resource Management
Support the evaluation and prioritization of new NPDI project intake across the four business units.
Coordinate with BU PMO leads to assess project scope, service involvement, resource requirements, and timing.
Maintain accurate project status, milestones, risks, dependencies, and resource information.
Identify capacity constraints and coordinate resource planning with Global Services leadership.
Support portfolio reporting and provide visibility into project health, progress, and emerging risks.
Contribute to continuous improvement of Global Services PMO processes, standards, and operating models.
Cross-Functional and Global Collaboration
Serve as the primary Global Services project contact for assigned NPDI initiatives.
Build strong working relationships with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, BU PMOs, and regional service leadership.
Facilitate alignment across global and regional stakeholders with competing priorities.
Ensure project decisions, actions, and dependencies are clearly communicated.
Promote consistency in service readiness and project execution across regions.
Support the development of global standards, playbooks, and repeatable implementation processes.
Digital Service and Technology Initiatives
Lead or support projects involving digital service capabilities, connected products, field technologies, and service transformation.
Coordinate cross-functional initiatives involving digital workflows, AI-enabled service tools, predictive maintenance, and connected service solutions.
Ensure technology initiatives address operational requirements and deliver measurable business value.
Partner with technical teams to manage implementation milestones, dependencies, and deployment readiness.
Support the integration of new technologies into global service operations.
Risk Management and Continuous Improvement
Maintain project risk, issue, action, and dependency registers.
Proactively identify schedule, resource, technical, operational, and service readiness risks.
Develop mitigation plans and coordinate timely resolution of project issues.
Capture lessons learned and incorporate improvements into future NPDI initiatives.
Drive improvements in project governance, execution discipline, and launch effectiveness.
Provide leadership with clear recommendations and escalation paths when project performance is at risk.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Project Management, Operations, or a related discipline.
5+ years of experience in project management, program management, operations, engineering, product development, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional projects.
Experience with new product introduction, product development, service operations, or technology implementation.
Strong project planning, execution, risk management, and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working with geographically distributed teams and multiple organizational functions.
Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a dynamic environment.
Strong written, verbal, and executive communication skills.
Ability to analyze complex problems, establish priorities, and drive actionable outcomes.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in critical infrastructure, data centers, power systems, thermal management, cooling technologies, or related industries.
Experience with NPDI, stage-gate governance, design transfer, or product lifecycle management.
Experience supporting global service organizations or regional capability development.
PMP certification or equivalent project management experience.
Lean Six Sigma certification or continuous improvement experience.
Experience managing digital transformation, field technology, or service technology projects.
Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Power BI, or similar project management tools.
Experience developing project governance frameworks, operating models, or PMO standards.

Core Competencies

Project Leadership: Ability to lead complex initiatives from planning through execution and launch.
Strategic Thinking: Ability to connect project activities to business priorities and global service strategy.
Execution Excellence: Strong ownership of timelines, deliverables, dependencies, and results.
Stakeholder Management: Ability to align cross-functional teams and influence without direct authority.
Risk Management: Ability to anticipate challenges and develop effective mitigation strategies.
Global Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across regions, cultures, and business units.
Communication: Ability to communicate project status, risks, and decisions clearly to technical and executive audiences.
Continuous Improvement: Commitment to improving project execution, governance, and service readiness.

Travel

Up to 25% travel, including domestic and international travel, based on project and business requirements.

Position Impact

This role ensures that Vertiv’s products, technologies, and service offerings are effectively integrated into global service operations. Through disciplined project execution, cross-functional alignment, and proactive risk management, the Global Services NPDI Project Manager helps reduce launch risk, improve service readiness, and accelerate the successful deployment of innovative solutions to customers worldwide.

About Us

The successful candidate will embrace Vertiv’s Core Principles & Behaviors to help execute our Strategic Priorities.

OUR CORE PRINCIPLES:
Safety. Integrity. Respect. Teamwork. Inclusion.

OUR STRATEGIC PRIORITIES

High-Performance Culture
Customer Focus
Operational Excellence
Innovation
Financial Strength

VERTIV BEHAVIORS

Own it
Act with urgency
Foster a customer-first mindset
Think big and execute
Lead by example
Drive continuous improvement
Learn and seek out development
Promote transparent & open communication

About Vertiv

Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to enable its customers’ vital applications to run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks, and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extend from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Westerville, Ohio, USA, Vertiv employs around 34,000 people and does business in more than 130 countries. Visit Vertiv.com to learn more.

Title:
Technical Project Manager
Location:

Role Summary:

We are seeking a Staff Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead complex, cross-portfolio technology initiatives within Global Product Technology, with a strong focus on Merch Planning, Forecasting, Sizing, and Allocation systems.
This role operates at the intersection of business and technology, owning delivery across multiple interdependent programs. The Staff TPM is responsible for driving end-to-end outcomes, shaping technical and business decisions, and ensuring planning and allocation capabilities deliver measurable business impact.
This role requires deep understanding of retail planning lifecycles, inventory flow, and allocation strategies, combined with the ability to orchestrate complex technology delivery at scale.

Key Responsibilities

1. Portfolio Ownership & Program Leadership

Own end-to-end delivery outcomes across multiple programs spanning Merch Planning, Sizing, Forecasting, Allocation, and Inventory Optimization
Drive alignment across Flowstate initiatives that support:

Forecast-driven size curves
In-season reforecasting
Allocation and transfer optimization
Ensure execution aligns to GTM gates, buy cycles, and merchandising decision timelines

2. Merch Planning & Allocation Business Acumen (Critical)

Serve as a thought partner to Merch Planning and Allocation leaders, translating business needs into scalable technology solutions
Deeply understand and incorporate:

Pre-season planning (assortment planning, size curves, buy quantities)
In-season management (reforecasting, transfers, sell-through optimization)
Allocation strategies across DCs and stores
Evaluate tradeoffs between:

Forecast accuracy vs responsiveness
Inventory optimization vs service levels
Automation vs planner control
Ensure technology solutions directly improve:

Forecast accuracy
Inventory productivity
Allocation efficiency
Time-to-decision for planners

3. Technical & Strategic Decision Leadership

Drive cross-system decision-making (architecture, sequencing, data flows, integration with planning tools like Anaplan, Snowflake, etc.)
Lead decision frameworks (options, tradeoffs, recommendations) for business and technology leadership
Ensure solutions reflect end-to-end planning workflows, not isolated system improvements
Act as a technical and business translator between Planning, Product, and Engineering

4. Release Governance & Delivery Management

Own and evolve release governance and readiness processes across planning and allocation systems
Ensure releases align to critical business windows (GTM, buys, peak seasons)
Drive proactive coordination of:

Data dependencies (forecast inputs, inventory signals)
Cross-system releases impacting planners
Prevent business disruption through tight release discipline and validation rigor

5. Delivery Excellence & Operating Model Design

Design and scale delivery operating models for planning systems across multiple teams
Standardize execution practices across:

Backlog readiness tied to business outcomes
Planning feature prioritization
Cross-team coordination
Lead initiatives to improve:

Delivery predictability
Feature adoption by business users
Quality of outputs used by planners

6. Cross-Functional Orchestration & Dependency Management

Act as the single-threaded owner connecting Merch Planning, Allocation, Engineering, Data, and Product teams
Manage dependencies across:

Forecasting engines
Sizing logic
Allocation and transfer systems
Surface and resolve risks tied to data quality, model outputs, and downstream planning impacts

7. Operational Excellence & Incident Leadership

Lead response to production issues impacting planning or allocation outcomes (forecast errors, allocation mismatches, data delays)
Drive root cause analysis with both technical and business context
Ensure continuous improvements in:

SLA adherence
Data accuracy and reliability
Planning system stability

8. Executive Influence & Stakeholder Leadership

Deliver executive-ready insights linking technology delivery to business outcomes (inventory, forecast accuracy, allocation effectiveness)
Influence prioritization decisions based on business value, not just delivery feasibility
Partner with senior leaders across:

Merch Planning
Allocation
Product
Engineering

9. Scalable Mechanisms & Organizational Impact

Build scalable mechanisms tailored to planning and allocation domains:
Forecast validation frameworks
Allocation readiness checklists
Dependency maps across data → models → planning tools
Enable teams to operate with clarity, accountability, and business alignment
Coach PMs/TPMs on connecting delivery execution to merchandising outcomes

Required Qualifications

8–12+ years in Technical Program Management or Program Management
Proven experience owning portfolio-level programs across planning, supply chain, or retail technology domains
Strong understanding of:

Merch Planning and Allocation processes
Forecasting and inventory optimization concepts
Cross-functional delivery in data-driven systems
Demonstrated ability to influence both technical and business leadership decisions

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Anaplan, planning systems, or allocation engines
Exposure to AI/ML-based forecasting or optimization models
Experience with data platforms (e.g., Snowflake) and end-to-end data pipelines
Background in retail, apparel, or omnichannel inventory environments

Education

Bachelor’s or Master’s of engineering, or related fields.

Role Overview

We are seeking a CCAR Finance Program Manager to lead the end-to-end delivery of the bank’s Finance stress testing platform, covering finance model execution, capital and balance sheet aggregation, and FR Y-14 regulatory reporting.

This role will drive the implementation and integration of key components of the CCAR finance architecture, including the Finance Model Execution Platform (MEP), enterprise aggregation engine, and regulatory reporting platforms (e.g., Axiom). The program manager will coordinate across Finance, Risk, Treasury, and Technology teams to ensure timely delivery, regulatory compliance, and alignment with enterprise stress testing requirements.

The ideal candidate will combine strong program management experience with deep understanding of CCAR, finance stress testing, and regulatory reporting frameworks.

Key Responsibilities

Program Leadership

Lead the end-to-end CCAR Finance program spanning model execution, aggregation, and regulatory reporting.
Manage delivery across multiple workstreams including Finance MEP, balance sheet and PPNR projections, aggregation, and FR Y-14 reporting.
Define program roadmap, milestones, and delivery plans aligned with regulatory timelines.
Coordinate across Finance, Risk, Treasury, and Technology stakeholders.

Model Execution Platform (MEP)

Oversee implementation of the Finance Model Execution Platform supporting execution of:
Balance sheet projection models
PPNR models
RWA and capital models
Tax and capital action models
Ensure integration with scenario management, data ingestion pipelines, and aggregation layers.

Aggregation

Lead the design and delivery of the CCAR aggregation framework to consolidate outputs from finance and risk models.
Ensure consistency across model outputs and alignment with enterprise stress testing assumptions.
Implement controls for data reconciliation, adjustments, overlays, and audit traceability.

Regulatory Reporting

Manage implementation and integration of FR Y-14 reporting processes including Axiom or similar regulatory platforms.
Ensure automated data feeds from aggregation to reporting templates.
Establish reconciliation controls between aggregation outputs, general ledger, and regulatory reports.

Governance and Regulatory Engagement

Establish program governance, delivery tracking, and issue management processes.
Coordinate with Model Risk Management, Internal Audit, and Regulatory Affairs.
Support regulatory submissions and examinations related to CCAR.

Stakeholder Management

Serve as the primary liaison between Finance, Risk, Technology, and external vendors.
Drive alignment across cross-functional teams delivering the CCAR platform.
Provide regular updates to senior finance and technology leadership.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in finance technology, regulatory reporting, or stress testing programs.
Strong knowledge of CCAR / DFAST regulatory frameworks and FR Y-14 reporting requirements.
Experience implementing finance model platforms, aggregation engines, or regulatory reporting systems.
Proven experience managing large cross-functional regulatory programs.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Axiom regulatory reporting platform.
Experience building or managing model execution platforms for finance or risk models.
Familiarity with balance sheet forecasting, PPNR modeling, RWA calculations, and capital planning.
Experience working with cloud data platforms (e.g., Databricks) and modern data architectures.
Prior experience working with regulators or regulatory remediation programs.

À propos de & Whitney Canada

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix

Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe ?

Vous contribuerez activement à la stratégie de gestion des risques et à l’évaluation des investissements industriels en fournissant des analyses rigoureuses, des recommandations éclairées et un soutien opérationnel aux projets stratégiques de l’entreprise.

Vous appuierez le directeur dans l’identification, l’analyse et le suivi des risques industriels et financiers, tout en contribuant à l’évaluation et à la gestion des projets d’investissement stratégiques.

Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil
du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien ?

Participer à l’élaboration des cartographies de risques et à la mise à jour des matrices d’évaluation.
Collecter, structurer et analyser les données financières et opérationnelles liées aux projets d’investissement.
Préparer des rapports d’analyse pour les comités de décision, incluant des recommandations chiffrées.
Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance des investissements (ROI, NPV, IRR).
Collaborer avec les équipes qualité, ingénierie, finance et juridique pour documenter les risques et les plans d’atténuation.
Contribuer aux audits internes et aux revues de conformité réglementaire.
Maintenir une veille sur les tendances du secteur, les évolutions réglementaires et les meilleures pratiques en gestion des risques.

Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir ?

Diplôme universitaire en gestion de projet, administration, ingénierie ou domaine connexe

TELUS Health is empowering every person to live their healthiest life. Guided by our vision, we are leveraging the power of our leading edge technology and focusing on the uniqueness of each individual to create the future of health. As a global-leading health and well-being provider – encompassing physical, mental and financial health – TELUS Health is improving health outcomes for consumers, patients, healthcare professionals, employers and employees.

Join Our Team

At TELUS Health, our Payroll Implementation team plays a critical role in enabling clients to operate efficiently, remain compliant, and deliver a better experience to their employees. We're building a function that combines deep functional expertise with genuine partnership—working alongside clients to redesign not just their systems, but how they operate. If you're someone who takes pride in solving complex problems and driving measurable operational improvements, you'll find this work meaningful.

Our team is collaborative and forward-thinking. We value continuous learning, excellence in execution, and the kind of partnership that turns challenging implementations into success stories. You'll work with talented Business Analysts, architects, and technical teams who care about getting it right.

The Impact You'll Make and What We'll Accomplish Together

Lead End-to-End Payroll Transformations

You'll own the complete payroll implementation journey—from understanding client requirements in discovery workshops to designing solutions, configuring systems, executing testing, and ensuring readiness for cutover. You won't just hand off work; you'll drive accountability and ensure every phase moves the client closer to success.

Solve Complex Payroll & Process Challenges

Every client's payroll operation is unique. You'll assess their business requirements against system capabilities, partner across teams (Solution Architecture, Product, Development, Data, QA) to design practical solutions, and use advanced SQL skills to validate configurations, analyze data, and investigate issues. You'll dig deep to find root causes and provide the evidence-based insights that drive confident decisions.

Champion Continuous Improvement

Beyond implementation, you'll help clients see their payroll operations with fresh eyes. You'll evaluate their current processes for inefficiencies, compliance risks, and opportunities—then design and recommend improved future-state processes that strengthen accuracy, scalability, and controls. You'll own the follow-through to ensure improvements stick and deliver measurable value.

Build Capability & Mentor

Others

You'll provide direction and coaching to Business Analysts and team members, promote best practices, and capture lessons learned to elevate the quality of future implementations. You'll be someone others turn to for guidance and clarity in uncertain situations.

Communicate with Clarity and Conviction

You'll translate complex payroll and technical concepts into language that resonates with both business and technical audiences. You'll facilitate workshops, document outcomes, drive decisions to resolution, and maintain strong client relationships through transparency and responsiveness.

You're the Missing Piece of the Puzzle

You bring:

Deep payroll expertise — You understand closed-loop payroll processes, payroll system architecture, configuration, and controls. You're fluent in payroll best practices and common implementation challenges.
Advanced SQL skills — You're comfortable analyzing payroll data, validating calculations, investigating exceptions, supporting data migrations, and providing evidence-based recommendations.
Hands-on configuration experience — You've configured major payroll or benefits systems (SAP, Workday, ADP, or equivalent) and understand how business requirements translate into system setup.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability — You can break down complex requirements, identify root causes, and drive solutions. You're comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy digging deeper.
Excellent communication skills — You can explain intricate payroll concepts clearly, guide teams through difficult decisions, facilitate alignment across stakeholders, and build trust through transparency.

$75K - $95K

We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, even if the posted salary range doesn't match your expectations. We're open to discussing competitive compensation packages tailored to your experience level and expertise.

Comprehensive total rewards package highlighting competitive salary and bonus structures, minimum 3 weeks of vacation, and flexible benefits plan to meet the needs of you and your family
Flexibility to work in-office, virtually or a combination of both
Generous company matched pension
Opportunity to give back to communities in which we work, live and serve
Career growth and learning & development opportunities to develop your skills
And much more…

Why This Opportunity

This is a role that balances deep technical expertise with strategic business impact. You'll work on meaningful transformations—helping clients reduce operational risk, improve compliance, and enhance the employee experience through better payroll operations. You'll grow your expertise in payroll systems, process design, and data analysis while mentoring other professionals. And you'll do it as a trusted advisor that clients genuinely rely on, not just as an implementer.

If you're a payroll expert who loves solving complex problems, driving continuous improvement, and building strong partnerships with clients—this is your role.

new_jobs.description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

Position Summary

The Senior Program Manager is responsible for leading a major workstream within a large, complex enterprise-wide transformation program. Reporting to the Sr. Director/Program Lead, this role is accountable for the day-to-day leadership, planning, coordination, execution oversight, and delivery management of an assigned workstream.

The Senior Program Manager will work closely with business, IT, functional leaders, and implementation partners to ensure the workstream is aligned to overall program objectives, integrated with related workstreams, and delivered on time and with quality. This role requires strong leadership, structure, and cross-functional coordination in a highly complex environment.

Key Responsibilities

Workstream Leadership

Lead an assigned workstream within the broader enterprise-wide transformation program
Own day-to-day planning, coordination, execution oversight, and delivery tracking for the workstream
Ensure workstream objectives, milestones, deliverables, and dependencies are clearly defined and actively managed
Drive accountability across team members and stakeholders to achieve committed outcomes

Planning and Execution

Develop and maintain detailed workstream plans, timelines, milestones, and action logs
Coordinate activities across business, IT, functional teams, and external implementation partners
Monitor progress against plan and proactively identify risks, issues, and delivery gaps
Drive timely resolution of blockers and escalate matters as appropriate

Risk, Issue, and Dependency Management

Identify, track, and manage workstream risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies
Partner with other workstream leads to address cross-functional impacts and integration points
Escalate critical risks and decisions to the Program Lead with recommended actions

Governance and Reporting

Prepare and provide regular status updates on workstream progress, milestones, risks, issues, and decisions
Support program governance forums by ensuring timely, accurate, and transparent reporting
Maintain documentation, decision logs, action items, and key workstream artifacts

Stakeholder Management

Build strong relationships with business, IT, and functional stakeholders across the assigned workstream
Partner with implementation teams and vendors to align on scope, deliverables, and timelines
Facilitate discussions, drive alignment, and support decision-making across stakeholders

Business Readiness and Adoption

Partner with business leads and change partners to support readiness, process alignment, and adoption activities
Help ensure the workstream is not only delivered from a technical perspective but is also operationally ready for implementation
Reinforce focus on business outcomes, user impact, and sustainable adoption

Quality and Delivery Discipline

Drive disciplined execution, issue resolution, and follow-through across the workstream
Ensure alignment with overall program governance, standards, templates, and reporting expectations
Support integrated planning and coordination with the broader transformation office and program leadership team

Financials/ Budget management

Lead workstream budget management, including actuals, forecast, accruals, and variance analysis.
Partner with Finance and PMO to maintain accurate financial reporting and forecast updates aligned to scope, resources, and delivery plans.
Drive disciplined, repeatable financial management processes aligned with program governance and financial best practices.
Identify, communicate, and help mitigate budget risks, forecast changes, and cost impacts across the workstream.
Ensure financial controls and documentation are audit-ready and able to withstand internal and external audit scrutiny.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required
8+ years of program or project management experience, including leadership of complex, cross-functional initiatives
Experience leading a major workstream within a large enterprise-wide transformation, ERP transformation, or similarly complex strategic program
Strong experience in integrated planning, risk management, issue resolution, and stakeholder coordination
Experience working across business and technology teams in a matrixed environment
Deep expertise in large scale Program budget management
Demonstrated ability to manage complexity, drive execution, and influence without direct authority
Strong written, verbal, and executive-level communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with large-scale ERP or enterprise transformation programs
Experience working with system integrators and third-party implementation partners
Familiarity with change management, business readiness, and adoption planning
PMP, Agile, or related certifications preferred
Experience in complex, highly regulated, or global environments is a plus

Key Competencies

Program and workstream leadership
Planning and execution management
Cross-functional coordination
Risk and issue management
Stakeholder engagement
Problem-solving and decision support
Communication and reporting
Accountability and follow-through

Success in This Role

Success in this role will be demonstrated through strong leadership of the assigned workstream, timely delivery of milestones and deliverables, proactive management of risks and dependencies, effective coordination across stakeholders, and clear contribution to the broader transformation program’s objectives and outcomes.

We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. new_jobs.title: Substation Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Electrical Consultants, Inc. (ECI) is a leading power engineering consultant firm that provides engineering, system planning and studies, technical consultation, project management, surveying, environmental planning, commissioning/testing and construction services to electric utilities, energy developers, and industrials throughout the U.S. Our experience includes system voltages from 4.16 kV through 765 kV.

ECI has an immediate opening for a Substation Project Manager in Cumberland or Augusta, Maine. Responsibilities include the conceptual, preliminary and final detailed design of new, upgraded, and expanded substations, including all aspects of engineering, material procurement, construction, and commissioning/startup support through energization. Additional responsibilities include the scoping, budgeting, scheduling, planning, executing, monitoring and reporting of substation projects and proposals. The Project Manager oversees a project team (or teams) of project and design engineers, designers, drafters, and support staff. Project Managers diligently execute ECI's quality control procedure, ensuring best-in class project execution and delivery. Project Managers are ECI's primary interface with clients and other project stakeholders. Project Managers provide technical mentorship and training of project team design staff.

Minimum Requirements:
Bachelor of Science or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering from an ABET accredited university, 10+ years' project engineering experience, or an acceptable combination of education and experience; 2+ years of substation project management experience; excellent verbal and written communication skills; strong organization and planning skills; commitment to quality and accuracy; and a willingness and ability to meet fast-paced project schedules. A PE license in at least one US state is required and PMP certification is preferred. The successful applicant must have an advanced knowledge of power engineering principals, understand applicable codes, standards and design tools, and have the ability to direct and oversee multiple technical disciplines in completion of substation projects. The successful applicant may be subject to client-mandated drug and background checking. Occasional travel/driving is required; therefore, the successful applicant will be subject to ECI's auto insurance carrier requirements. Applicants must not require sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B visa status) now or in the future.

Compensation Range: $130,000 - $170,000 Annually

Salary Commensurate With Experience And Education. Benefits Include

Medical, dental and vision insurance
Flexible spending account
Health savings account
Life insurance
Disability insurance
401(k), profit sharing and employee stock ownership plan
Paid vacation, personal days and holidays
Paid Parental Leave
Continued professional education reimbursement

Electrical Consultants, Inc. (ECI) employs over 850 engineers, designers, project managers, surveyors, ROW agents, environmental planners, construction professionals and support staff in 37 offices across the U.S. The firm has more than 40 years of experience in the planning, engineering, and construction of a wide range of power delivery projects including substations, transmission lines, distribution systems, communication systems and industrial facilities.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn.

What We Are Looking For

As a Staff Technical Program Manager (Release Management), you will report to the Manager of Release Management and join our Software Product-Design team. This is a senior individual contributor (IC) role that balances strategic release architecture and automation with hands-on, day-to-day release train execution. We are hiring for this role to help drive scale and automation in our release operations for predictive prevention, establishing robust automated release gating as our commercial driverless fleet scales from a dozen vehicles to thousands. This is a high-impact opportunity for a force multiplier who thrives on combining hands-on tactical execution with long-term operational scale. You are highly motivated to remove manual friction, manage release operations, and automate software release and deployment frameworks in a safety-critical, high-velocity environment.

In this role you will

Lead Day-to-Day Release Operations & Cadence: Own and execute the end-to-end release cycle, including orchestrating regular release train schedules, managing branch cut-offs, running daily release/build triage, and coordinating hotfix deployments across software and vehicle platforms.
Cross-Functional Coordination & Release Communication: Serve as the primary operational hub for release readiness, driving daily alignment across engineering, safety, hardware, and test operations teams while maintaining transparent release communications and dashboards.
Drive Predictive Prevention and Release Automation: Shift release operations toward predictive prevention by identifying and eliminating manual friction points, automating release workflows, and utilizing AI/ML tools for triage classification and anomaly detection.
Establish Data-Driven Release Gating: Help architect and maintain automated "Release Gates" that auto-assemble compliance evidence using structured data (Single Source of Truth), ensuring rigorous quality and safety standards before release promotion.
Manage High-Scale Branching & Change Control: Govern and orchestrate concurrent release branches across diverse customers, hardware configurations, and Operational Design Domains (ODDs), maintaining absolute branching hygiene and change control.
Ensure Safety-First Rigor and Auditable Compliance: Treat release documentation and launch reports with software-grade discipline—ensuring version control, complete auditability, and safety compliance without introducing operational bottlenecks.

Required Qualifications

7+ Years of Hands-On Release Experience: Technical program management, release engineering, or systems engineering background with direct, day-to-day release train execution and managing software-hardware integrations in complex environments.
Safety-Critical Domain Expertise: Experience working under strict safety-regulated standards (such as ISO 26262, DO-178C, or ISO 13485) within automotive, aerospace, medical or robotics, with strong configuration management, baseline, and change control practices.
Tactical Build & CI/CD Execution: Practical, hands-on technical experience with CI/CD build automation tools (e.g., Buildkite, GitHub Actions) and monorepo build systems (e.g., Bazel) to troubleshoot and execute daily release operations at scale.
Complex Branching & Daily Triage: Proven track record of orchestrating concurrent release branches, running hands-on daily build/release triage, and executing hotfix deployments across diverse teams and hardware platforms.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Governance: Collaborative track record of partnering across engineering, safety, hardware, and test operations teams to establish transparent governance, shared release visibility, and cross-team trust.
Customer & Team Support Mindset: Strong team player willing to support internal operations, external partners, and high-priority releases with occasional evening or weekend coverage as needed.
Travel Requirement: Ability to travel to engineering centers in Mountain View, CA, Terminal Operations in Texas or Pittsburgh, PA as business needs arise.

Desirable Qualifications

AV & Robotics Background: Direct, hands-on experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, machine learning systems, or complex cyber-physical environments.
AI-Leveraged Release Operations: Practical experience applying ML/AI tooling to day-to-day release operations, such as automated test-failure classification, triage automation, or pipeline anomaly detection.
Automation-First & Collaborative Mindset: Passion for building self-service release tooling and reducing operational friction while fostering seamless cross-functional alignment and developer enablement.
Cloud & SaaS Infrastructure: Practical familiarity with cloud environments (AWS) and progressive deployment methodologies (feature flagging, progressive delivery, service dependency ordering).
Proactive Execution & Planning: Proven capability to manage day-to-day edge cases and unknown release risks by establishing team-wide visibility and proactive build health tracking.

For roles based in San Francisco, CA and Mountain View, CA: The salary range for this position is $181,000 - $290,000 per year.

For roles based in Pittsburgh, PA: The salary range for this position is $163,000 - $261,000 per year.

Aurora’s pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, qualifications, relevant education or training, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future. The successful candidate will also be eligible for an annual bonus, equity compensation, and benefits.

Working at Aurora

At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks.

We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, we operate in a hybrid work environment where Aurorans are in office at least 3 days per week.

Our Careers page provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom.

Our commitment to safety

At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what.

Our commitment to inclusion

Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at careersiteaccommodations@aurora.tech.

new_jobs.description:
"Stepping into the Implementations Team Lead role has been an incredibly rewarding experiences in my career. It’s a position that has truly helped me grow—both professionally and personally. The role fosters collaboration, encourages continuous learning, and is backed by an incredibly supportive and focused team. If you're looking for a leadership opportunity where you're empowered to make an impact and surrounded by people who lift each other up, I would absolutely recommend this role!"
~ Britnee Themann - Team Lead, Implementations

As an Implementation Project Manager at Absorb, you're the linchpin for our clients, ensuring they grasp the ins and outs of our cutting-edge product. Your role? To guarantee their seamless transition to our LMS. Acting as their main point of contact, project manager, guide, and educator, you'll drive client success by sharing your expert knowledge, offering best practice guidance, troubleshooting any implementation hurdles, and overseeing the complete rollout of the Absorb LMS. Simply put, you will elevate our client experiences and propel our technology forward!

Absorb Culture - Absorb LMS

What You’ll Do

Own the software implementation process (average duration of 8 weeks) for new clients, end-to-end via phone, by email, and/or virtual meetings.
Gather and document requirements, confirm project scope, and work with clients to develop achievable timelines and program goals.
Act as a client partner and liaison for cross-departmental collaboration and resource management.
Support and implement additional products and integrations such as RESTful API, CRM/HRM integrations, etc.
Provide in-depth training on our LMS (Learning Management System), including best practices and workflows customized to each client’s needs.
Manage a portfolio of projects, maintaining a high level of quality while coordinating multiple projects at once.

What You’ll Bring

4+ years in Client Onboarding or Implementation and Project Management, working in software implementations, or similar experience.
Previous training experience / software training experience.
Understanding of basic online/SaaS (Software as a Service) concepts.
Proven time management skills.
Project oriented mindset.

Additional Preferred Qualifications

Previous LMS admin or training experience.
Knowledge in the adult learning and E-learning industry
PMP or formal project management experience.
Previous experience working with data import tools.

Technologies We Use

Absorb LMS, Salesforce, ChurnZero, Monday.com, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Office, Gong

Are you ready to become an Absorber?

What We Offer

Fully remote-first work with flexible work arrangements 🏡
Comprehensive Health and Wellness Benefits including retirement savings programs, eligibility for two different bonus plans, generous time off, comprehensive medical and dental benefits based on your country of location 🧘
New Hire Equipment Allowance and monthly Flex Allowance to support your success 📦
Endless opportunity for career growth and internal mobility 🌱
Employee driven DE&I programs 🫶

Who are we?

Absorb Software is the leading global AI-driven learning platform provider, helping organizations unlock the full potential of their workforce. With its innovative Strategic Learning Systems (SLS) approach, Absorb empowers businesses to align learning with strategic goals, driving measurable impact and workforce agility. The Absorb LMS platform delivers personalized, scalable, and engaging learning experiences for employees, customers, and partners worldwide. Trusted by over 3,300 organizations and 34 million users, Absorb is redefining the future of workplace learning through cutting-edge AI, seamless integrations, and an unwavering commitment to innovation. We empower learners to enrich their lives, workplaces and communities.

Our Values Are Simple

We achieve exceptional results by genuinely caring about each other and the work we do
We’re united, and we grow through our commitment to elevating continual learning!

AI @ Absorb

We believe in the power of AI and technology to make learning accessible to everyone. By exploring new tools and constantly experimenting, we’re redefining what’s possible. We take an AI‑first approach to unlock human potential, drive impact, and scale better outcomes. As the world evolves, Absorb is committed to growing with you. Investing in your skills every step of the way.

We use AI tools to support our recruitment process, such as organizing applications and highlighting potential matches based on role requirements. While these tools help streamline our review, all screening and final hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team. We encourage candidates to apply authentically and not rely solely on AI-generated responses in their applications.

Absorb is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment for all our people. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications. Should you require any accommodation during the recruitment process, please indicate this on your application and we will work with you to meet your accessibility needs. For any questions, please contact us at accessiblecareers@absorblms.com

Successful candidates for this position will be subject to pre-employment background screening, including a criminal record check and must be able to show proof of legal eligibility to work in the country they have applied to without sponsorship.

Job Description:

Discover a career that is challenging, impactful, and mission critical. Join our team as an All Source Intelligence Analyst and make an impact in expanding a newly formed protective intelligence unit. While you help us advance the mission, we’ll help advance your career.

At GDIT, people are our differentiator. As an Intelligence Analyst, you will help ensure today is safe and tomorrow is smarter. Our work depends on a highly motivated Analysts joining our team to provide administrative and technical support to law enforcement and threat intelligence operations that support the highest levels of government. When we succeed, you succeed and together our best becomes better.

HOW THE INTELLIGENCE ANALYST WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

Collects and analyzes information attained from open source resources in addition to: Federal, State, and local law enforcement agencies, the intelligence community, foreign governments, financial institutions, and technology companies.
Identifies intelligence sources to support law enforcement missions and performs assessments to determine pattern of life attributes and the identity of threat actors.
Has knowledge of forensic analysis of digital information and uses forensically sound procedures to assist in threat investigations using the internet and digital devices as a primary or peripheral means.
Is familiar with forensic tools and techniques used to recover and evaluate metadata from various sources, and works in conjunction with analysts to detect steganography, and recovers deleted, fragmented or corrupted data from digital media of all types.
Observes proper evidence custody and control procedures (chain of custody), documents procedures and findings in a manner suitable for inclusion in criminal investigations and courtroom presentation, and prepares comprehensive written notes and reports.
Utilizes common cyber intelligence tools and software to search and collect publicly available information from the internet and dark web for threats against government personnel, facilities and operations.
Prepares formal assessments and briefs to various levels of government leadership in a manner that is easy to understand and demonstrates logical, supportable conclusions and relationships.
Works closely with government liaisons to leverage agency resources, strengthen communication and collaboration, and capture best practices and lessons learned.
Supports the protection mission by coordinating closely with law enforcement personnel and providing proactive analysis for all missions, including domestic and international travel.
Prepares and conducts routine training for the government’s personnel covering various aspects of the criminal intelligence process and its ability to enhance contributions to the overall policing and protection mission.
Keeps abreast of emerging technologies and professional developments to remain current in the field and for application to work assignments.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:

Education: Bachelor's Degree
Required Experience: 4+ years of experience in intelligence operations in support of a law enforcement mission; all source analysis; understanding/knowledge of darknet ecosystems; experience using cyber tools/techniques to gather intelligence in support of threat/criminal investigations; coordinating with state/federal law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
Required Technical Skills: Experience with Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Publisher; experience with a variety of OSINT research tools.
Security Clearance Level: Active Top Secret with SCI Eligibility
Required Skills and Abilities: Excellent oral and written communication skills; attention to detail; knowledge and skill to adapt and apply various analytical and quantitative techniques and to document and justify recommendations; ability to establish and maintain relationships with key internal and external individuals/groups; gather, analyze, and present facts; interpret and apply rules, regulations and procedures.
Preferred Skills: Self-motivated and detail oriented.
Location: On Customer Site, Washington DC. Limited telework.

401K with company match

Internal mobility team dedicated to helping you own your career

Cutting-edge technology you can learn from
Rest and recharge with paid vacation and holidays

new_jobs.title: Information Security Analyst III
new_jobs.description:
Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse’s mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace.

About The Role

As an Information Security Analyst IIIyou will identify, investigate, contain, and help resolve security incidents while developing and improving enterprise detection capabilities. You will translate threat intelligence, attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures into applicable monitoring, analytics, and response workflows across security platforms. The analyst serves as a senior technical resource between IT, Information Security, Legal, Data Privacy, HR, and business partners, providing clear findings, risk context, and recommendations.

You will report to the Global Incident Response Supervisor and be located at Cranberry Township, PA. Hybrid work schedule.

Key Responsibilities

Respond to and investigate computer security incidents observing established incident response policies, plans, and procedures, including evaluation, scoping, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident analysis.
Analyze problematic activity reported by security technologies and partners, including IT, HR, Legal, and Data Privacy, and maintain complete, accurate investigation case records.
Develop, validate, implement, and maintain detection use cases, analytics, alerts, reports, and dashboards in security monitoring platforms to identify potential threats and vulnerabilities.
Translate current threat intelligence and attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures into threat models, detection logic, investigation guidance, and response actions.
Plan, test, tune, and refine detection content to improve accuracy, coverage, and operational value while reducing false positives and unnecessary analyst workload.
Provide technical guidance to first responders and other security operations personnel during investigations and major incidents, including on-call support.
Provide relevant, and audience-appropriate incident updates, investigation findings, risk assessments, metrics, and recommendations to partners and decision makers.
Maintain the operational effectiveness and configuration of assigned security solutions, including Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Sentinel, SIEM, SOAR, forensic, and threat intelligence technologies.
Collaborate with security operations, threat intelligence, engineering, architecture, and teams to define requirements and improve detection and response capabilities.
Perform other responsibilities and special projects as assigned.

Key responsibilities include triaging and remediating data incidents, performing data analysis, training new users, and performing impact analysis stemming from data updates. Job expectations include helping in defining access and ownership of data by domain, conducting quality control, and overseeing data maintenance.

Line of Business Description:

About Sanctions Screening Center of Excellence: The Center of Excellence for economic sanctions monitoring is part of Global Payment Operations (GPO). GPO is the central hub for Bank of America in playing a monumental and mission critical role in establishing, servicing, supporting and monitoring two of the most widely used electronic payment processing vehicles – Wire and ACH – in the financial services arena worldwide. GPO is also accountable for the SSCoE (Sanctions Screening Center of Excellence) that reviews all of Bank of America’s customers and transactions to ensure compliance with Bank of America’s Economic Sanctions Program. SSCoE serves BAML’s eight lines of business, delivering global, regional and local capabilities through secure, fast and reliable technology, and people with the knowledge and experience to deliver timely and accurate review of all sanctions alerts across all products of Bank of America. Team also has the responsibility to provide support to client facing teams and clients where needed to educate on compliance program, drive better quality of data defining the customer and their day-to-day banking transactions.

Manage the multiple on-going initiatives by attending calls from various projects, understand the Sanctions needs from the projects, Provide requirements to the projects and track the status of these projects.
Analyze alerts on a daily basis to chalk out strategies to reduce the false-positives, using different pattern matching and trending techniques

Develops, manages, and executes on controls, ensuring tracking, monitoring, and resolution of any control breaches with data platform

1 President's Choice Circle, Brampton, ON L6Y 5S5 (near Highway 407 and Mississauga Road)

North York Location:
243 Consumers Rd, North York, ON M2J 4W8 (near Highway 401 and Highway 404)

Lifemark Health Group (LHG) is a market leader in customized healthcare solutions. With over 20 years of service excellence, LHG is one of the largest, most trusted, and most comprehensive providers in Canada. As a national healthcare company, LHG employs over 5,000 highly trained clinicians, medical experts and team members in almost 400 locations coast-to-coast and continues to grow both organically as well as through acquisitions. With that growth, is a vision to be the most innovative healthcare providers in community rehabilitation, workplace health and wellness and medical assessment services. Lifemark was acquired by Loblaw Companies on May 10, 2022.

Lifemark Health Group is seeking a Senior Information Security Analyst
for a permanent, full-time role on our Security Team. In this position, you will monitor and respond to security threats across our systems, analyze security events, and help implement improvements. You will facilitate phishing awareness campaigns to strengthen organizational security posture, update security policies and playbooks to reflect evolving best practices and collaborate effectively with teams throughout the Lifemark network and its affiliates to ensure our information security practices support business goals. You will proactively identify risks through regular assessments, participate in incident response activities, and stay up to date with emerging technologies and threats to drive continuous improvement.

About You:

You are a seasoned information security professional with a passion for safeguarding technology and data. You bring strong technical expertise, extensive hands-on experience, and a commitment to continuous learning in the ever-evolving field of cybersecurity. Thriving in fast-paced environments, you excel at managing multiple priorities while maintaining attention to detail and high standards. Your collaborative approach allows you to work effectively across diverse teams, translating complex technical concepts into practical business solutions. Above all, you are dedicated to advancing Lifemark’s security posture and supporting its mission through proactive problem-solving and innovation.

Impact we're looking for you to make:

The role requires an in-depth understanding of Information Security practices as well as a good understanding of Microsoft products (such as Windows, Outlook/Exchange/O365), vulnerability management, anti-virus, identity & access management, network operations (proxy servers, DNS, firewalls, WAN/LAN switches), databases and exposure to DLP systems (such as Proofpoint and Palo Alto).

Involvement in the implementation of new security solutions, including participation in the creation and maintenance of policies, standards, baselines, guidelines, and procedures
Conduct vulnerability audits and assessments and participate in investigations, design, and execution of vulnerability assessments
Monitor computer networks and systems for security issues, penetration tests, and security audits; document any security issues or breaches in line with Lifemark’s information security policies, procedures, and guidelines
Respond to security alerts and work with the appropriate teams to investigate, triage, and resolve issues
Maintain documentation of support processes and infrastructure
Support incident and problem management, escalation, and resolution activities
Implement and test changes in accordance with Change Management procedures
Maintain a commitment to keeping current on the latest technologies, threats, and best practices through training courses and industry events
Manage Helpdesk Tier II/III requests pertaining to information security
Maintain relevant baselines and operational configurations, and review logs for the secure configuration and operation of server, compute, and network devices
Participate in the planning and design of enterprise security architecture, Business Continuity Plan (BCP), and Disaster Recovery (DR) plan
Provide input toward RFPs and security due diligence documents
Participate in client security audits, evidence collection, and tracking of remediation items
Own and track cybersecurity remediation activities aligned with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, including control-gap validation, evidence collection, action owners, target dates, risk acceptance, and reporting of overdue items
Conduct periodic access and configuration reviews covering privileged accounts, non-human identities, break-glass accounts, firewall rules, cloud service access, and other high-risk controls; document evidence and follow remediation to closure
Perform security reviews of new technologies, vendors, and material changes; document risks, minimum control requirements, and recommendations before implementation or renewal
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the IT security industry, including awareness of new or revised security solutions, improved security processes, and emerging attacks and threat vectors
Recommend additional security solutions or enhancements to existing security solutions to improve overall enterprise security
Participate in the deployment, integration, and configuration of new security solutions and enhancements to existing security solutions in accordance with standard operating procedures and enterprise security documentation
Provide after-hours and on-call support when needed

What we're looking for:

Minimum five years of progressive, hands-on information security experience, including at least two years independently leading security investigations, remediation initiatives, or security control operations in a complex enterprise environment.
Experience with network applications, firewall security, virtual private networking, and SIEM
Experience with cloud hosting platforms (Microsoft Azure preferred)
Knowledge of network and host IDS/IPS
Strong familiarity with data classification concepts and processes
Solid understanding of data loss and data protection processes
Experience with a wide variety of technical solutions focused on data protection and cybersecurity
Experience with Microsoft server and cloud infrastructure, such as Windows Server and Active Directory
Experience with Microsoft 365 security and collaboration tools, including Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Defender, Entra ID, and Purview
Demonstrated experience applying the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and translating framework gaps into prioritized, measurable remediation plans; experience supporting SOC 2 - comparable assurance activities is an asset
Experience assessing third-party, SaaS, and application security risks, including identity and access, data protection, logging, vulnerability management, resilience, and contractual security requirements
Experience in healthcare, another regulated environment, or a large distributed organization is strongly preferred; working knowledge of PHIPA, PIPEDA, and protection of personal health information is an asset
Excellent time management skills
Strong written and verbal communication
Work with different divisions understanding their IT Security needs
Set clear expectations and define key performance indicators for self
Work within a team environment providing insight when appropriate
Superior organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks
Ability to successfully interact with non-technical business contacts
Ability to analyze and understand technical information
Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment
Ability to conduct research into IT security issues and products as required

Additional Qualifications:

Associate degree in a related technical field or equivalent experience
Network+, Security+, GISP, MCSA, CISSP with demonstrated knowledge of security frameworks or standards such as CIS top 20, NIST and ISO 27001 (certifications are assets)
Understanding of remote management tools and techniques
Extensive knowledge of Microsoft Windows operating systems and Office 365
An understanding of network topologies and protocols (including firewalls, routers, switches, access points)
Experience with Microsoft Active Directory and PowerShell Scripting
Some knowledge of Microsoft windows server platform
Use of SAST/DAST tools such as Snyki.io, Fortify and Burp Suite
Use of work item tracking software such as Azure DEVOPS, Zendesk, ServiceNow and JIRA
Familiarity working with SQL databases schema, queries, entries, creation
Must be able to participate in a defined after-hours incident escalation rotation and support urgent cyber events when required.

Our Perks:

Have access to a yearly education re-imbursement fund
Receive 30% discount from Shopper Drug Mart purchases
Contribute to an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) with employer matching percentage
Have paid vacation days as well as wellness days
Have a choice to enroll in our Health & Dental Flex Life Benefits (or in lieu contribute to your RRSPs)
Access to employee assistance program
On-site gym, Basketball & Volleyball courts, Groceries delivered to work via PC Express, Dry-Cleaning services (1 Presidents Choice Circle Office)

new_jobs.description:
Job Title: Network Security Analyst 2

Location: 701 W 51st St Austin, TX 78751.

Onsite/Remote/Hybrid: Onsite

Contract/Perm: Full Time

Project Scope:

The Network Security Analyst II performs advanced cybersecurity and network security analysis work in support of clients enterprise security operations. This role is responsible for monitoring, detecting, investigating, and responding to security events across on-premises, cloud, and endpoint environments. The ideal candidate is a hands-on security operations professional with strong experience across SIEM, SOAR, EDR, network detection, and incident response platforms. This role requires sound judgment, technical depth, attention to detail, and a strong commitment to protecting clients systems, data, and services that support the health and well-being of Texans.
Roles/Responsibilities:

A network security analyst ensures that information systems and computer networks are secure. This includes protecting the company against hackers and cyber-attacks, as well as monitoring network traffic and server logs for activity that seems unusual.
Additionally, these analysts are responsible for finding vulnerabilities in the computer networks and creating recommendations for how to minimize these vulnerabilities.
The network security analyst investigates security breaches, develops strategies for any security issues that arise, and utilizes the help of firewalls and antivirus software to maintain security.
Monitor security alerts, logs, network events, endpoint telemetry, and threat intelligence feeds.
Analyze suspicious activity, anomalous network behavior, malware indicators, endpoint detections, and SIEM correlation events to determine scope, impact, and required response actions.
Perform incident triage, investigation, escalation, containment coordination, and documentation in alignment with HHSC security operations procedures.
Develop, tune, and maintain detection rules, dashboards, alerts, playbooks, and queries to improve visibility across network, endpoint, identity, and cloud environments.
Support threat hunting activities using KQL, SPL, packet/session analysis, endpoint telemetry, and other investigative techniques.
Assist with vulnerability, risk, and control assessments for network security infrastructure and enterprise information systems.
Document findings, prepare incident reports, track corrective actions, and communicate technical information to security leadership and business stakeholders.
Collaborate with network, infrastructure, cloud, endpoint, and application teams to validate security events and implement risk mitigation measures.
Maintain awareness of emerging cyber threats, attack techniques, indicators of compromise, and security best practices relevant to healthcare and public-sector environments.
Support compliance, audit, and reporting activities by providing evidence, metrics, and security operations documentation as requested.
Participate in incident response, escalation, and after-action review activities as needed.
Support enterprise security monitoring for systems that process, store, or transmit sensitive information.
Follow HHSC policies, procedures, standards, and applicable state and federal security requirements.
Maintain accurate operational documentation, investigation notes, metrics, and leadership-ready summaries.
May be required to provide support outside normal business hours during high-priority security incidents or planned maintenance activities.

Mandatory Skills:

4-7 years of experience in the field or in a related area. Familiar with standard concepts, practices, and procedures within a particular field. Relies on limited experience and judgment to plan and accomplish goals. A certain degree of creativity and latitude is required. Works under limited supervision with considerable latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment. Ability to maintain the security and integrity of critical infrastructure systems by preventing unauthorized access and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations related to national security and foreign ownership restrictions.
Minimum of seven years of experience in cybersecurity, network security, security operations, incident response, or a closely related information security role.
Hands-on experience with Microsoft Sentinel, including incident management, analytics rules, workbooks, automation, data connectors, and Kusto Query Language.
Experience using SIEM for log analysis, alert investigation, dashboarding, correlation searches, and security monitoring.
Experience with NDR for network traffic analysis, packet/session investigation, threat detection, and incident support.
Experience with EDR tools, including endpoint alert triage, device investigation, advanced hunting, and response actions.
Working knowledge of network security concepts, including firewalls, IDS/IPS, proxy logs, DNS, VPN, TCP/IP, segmentation, and secure network architecture.
Ability to analyze complex security events, correlate data across multiple sources, and produce clear written documentation and recommendations.
Knowledge of security frameworks, standards, and regulatory considerations such as NIST, CIS Controls, HIPAA, and state information security requirements.
Strong communication, collaboration, problem-solving, and analytical skills.
7 years of Knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, EDR, XDR, NDR
7 years of Experience with security log collection and management
7 years of Experience with threat intelligence concepts
7 years of Skill in writing and interpreting KQL, SPL, and security queries to support investigations and reporting
7 years of Experience in SIEM platform/architecture support
7 years of Experience in detection engineering methodology and implementation

Desirable Skills:

Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, information technology, or a related field. Relevant experience may be considered in place of education where applicable.
Microsoft security certifications are strongly preferred, such as Microsoft Certified: Security Operations Analyst Associate, Microsoft Certified: Cybersecurity Architect Expert, Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate, or Microsoft 365 Defender-related certifications.
Additional preferred certifications include CompTIA Security+, CySA+, GIAC security certifications, CISSP, CISM, CISA, Splunk Core Certified Power User, Splunk Enterprise Security Certified Admin, or SentinelOne product certifications.
10 years of Knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, EDR, XDR, NDR
10 years of Experience with security log collection and management
10 years of Experience with threat intelligence concepts
10 years of Skill in writing and interpreting KQL, SPL, and security queries to support investigations and reporting
10 years of Experience in SIEM platform/architecture support
10 years of Experience in detection engineering methodology and implementation

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, EDR, XDR, network detection and response, log management, and threat intelligence concepts.
Skill in writing and interpreting KQL, SPL, and security queries to support investigations and reporting.
Skill in identifying indicators of compromise, attacker tactics, suspicious network patterns, and endpoint-based threats.
Ability to prioritize alerts, document investigative steps, and escalate incidents based on severity and business impact.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a security operations environment with shifting priorities and time-sensitive incidents.
Ability to communicate cybersecurity risks, findings, and recommended actions to both technical and non-technical audiences.
